page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the weak category, with single-threaded gzip compression registering as poor. However, the instance leverages its 32 dedicated cores to achieve average multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression speeds. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also demonstrate average tier performance, aligning with its memory-optimized design.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.8xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its processing cores, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require top-tier single-threaded compute performance. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-core efficiency, meaning sequential processing tasks will experience bottlenecks. Additionally, the lack of bundled local storage requires users to factor in the performance of external block storage.

This instance is well-suited for workloads that demand substantial memory capacity but can tolerate moderate CPU performance. Appropriate use cases include in-memory databases, caching layers such as Redis, multi-threaded data processing, and medium-scale database operations. It is also capable of handling static web serving and moderate LLM inference tasks for smaller models.
